response: {"title":"Invariant differential probe","intervention":"Before finalizing, use at most 10% of the deadline for one differential probe comparing pre-change and post-change behavior on an input whose result should remain invariant, prioritizing an input that traverses the most edited modules.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, one bounded invariant differential probe will improve hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses, median wall_time, or turns by more than 5%.","mechanism":"A pre/post oracle detects unintended regressions without requiring the agent to derive an exact expected value, and maximizing edited-module traversal raises the chance of exposing composition errors.","assumptions":["A pre-change executable state or equivalent output is available","At least one relevant behavior should remain invariant","The probe can execute within the cap"],"risks":["The agent may choose behavior that was intended to change","The old behavior may already be incorrect","Environment nondeterminism may create false differences","Restoring or invoking the pre-change state may add overhead"],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks to the appended instruction or no instruction with identical model, seed, tools, repository state, and deadline; evaluate hidden tests and on-time completion.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment increases pass_rate, does not increase deadline-miss rate, and keeps median wall_time and turns no more than 5% above control."},"single_shot_ordinal":8}
